author: Aaronjacobs000
notes: For Kiteworks activity (secure email, file sharing, SFTP, MFT and web forms) sent over syslog to the data collector, in JSON Format or plain text, or by Kiteworks PubSub webhooks (Kiteworks 9.4.0 or later) straight to HTTP Ingest with the webhook's Token set to Bearer <HTTP Ingest key>, so no bridge is needed. The README has the steps. Sign-ins (user_logged_in, admin_logged_in, login), failed sign-ins, lockouts, unlocks, and password resets and changes go to Auth with the user, address, user agent, client, session and Kiteworks' error message. JSON records where a scan flagged a file (data.malicious, data.prohibited or data.quarantined) go to Thirdparty with the scan type, verdict, file and reason, high severity for a malicious file. Everything else goes to CloudAudit with the event name, the object type (or the plain text Activity Group) as the event type, the user and address, the file or folder path, the objects as resources, and a secure mail's subject, recipients and attachments as request parameters. Downloads and views are read-only. The syslog time is read as UTC, so set the Kiteworks syslog time zone to UTC. PubSub events use created. Kiteworks documents the PubSub envelope, a login example and the payload keys, and doesn't publish its syslog formats. The syslog JSON keys come from the Cortex XSIAM Kiteworks modeling rule (MIT), the event names from Exabeam's Kiteworks parsers (Apache-2.0), and the plain text line from Hunters' sample and those parsers. Made up in the samples: the PubSub upload and download event names (taken from Kiteworks' activity API examples), the value in brackets after the user ID and the sign-in Activity Groups in plain text, and the scan record. Appliance system lines (auditd, sendmail) aren't claimed. No built-in parser claimed these lines in 3 Parse Message runs. The children, combined with the parent into one parser, passed Run Test in a lab tenant on 2026-10-27 (244 of 244 fields matched the emulator in each of 3 runs), and the parent's confirm string picked the same lines there. Each child also passed Run Test as a separate parser under its parent (244 of 244 fields, each line taken in 5 of 5 runs). The PubSub route hasn't been tested end to end through HTTP Ingest.
